title: The beavers: exercises
subtitle: Five exercises on the text
label: Exercises
review: Written by Claude from the lesson text. Check the English and the answers before using it with learners.

items.q: Beavers use their strong front teeth to cut down small trees.
The dam makes the flowing water faster.
The entrance to the lodge is on the roof.
Where does the beaver family live?
items.why: “Deep in a beautiful forest, a family of beavers lives beside a little stream.”

items.q: What do beavers put in their dam?
items.why: “They put branches and sticks into the water. Then they add mud, stones, and more wood.”

items.q: What is a beaver's home called?
items.why: “They build a home called a lodge.”

items.q: What are beavers called in the text?
items.why: “These remarkable builders are called nature's engineers!”

blocks.title: 4. Open questions
blocks.note: These questions are open. Talk about your answers with your teacher or a classmate.

items.q: Without looking at the text, sum it up in three sentences.
items.model: Beavers cut wood with their strong teeth and build dams across streams. The dam slows the water, and a pond forms behind it. The beavers build a lodge with an underwater entrance, and their pond is a home for many other animals.

items.q: How do beavers build a dam?
items.model: They put branches and sticks into the water. Then they add mud, stones and more wood. Little by little, a strong dam forms.

items.q: Why is deep water good for beavers?
items.model: It helps protect them from animals that might hurt them. They can swim safely around their home.

items.q: Which other animals enjoy the beavers' pond?
items.model: Fish swim in the water, frogs rest near the pond, and ducks and other birds visit too.

items.q: Is there a river or a pond near your home? What animals live there?

blocks.title: 5. Put in order
blocks.intro: Put the events in the order of the story.
items: The beavers cut down small trees with their teeth
They build a dam across the stream
A pond forms behind the dam
They build a lodge with an underwater entrance
Fish, frogs and ducks come to the pond
